ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, this is a device designed by an extracurricular research group that can be used to measure the rotational speed of a turntable. Above the device is a ruler fixed together with the turntable and having transverse uniform graduations. A small ball with a hole is threaded on a smooth thin rod and connected to a light spring; the other end of the spring is fixed on the rotating shaft. The small ball can slide freely along the rod and rotate with the turntable in a horizontal plane. When the turntable is not rotating, the pointer points at O; when the angular velocity of the turntable's rotation is ω1, the pointer points at A; when the angular velocity of the turntable's rotation is ω2, the pointer points at B. Suppose none of the springs exceeds the elastic limit. Then the ratio of ω1 to ω2 is (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, this is a device designed by an extracurricular research group that can be used to measure the rotational speed of a turntable. Above the device is a ruler fixed together with the turntable and having transverse uniform graduations. A small ball with a hole is threaded on a smooth thin rod and connected to a light spring; the other end of the spring is fixed on the rotating shaft. The small ball can slide freely along the rod and rotate with the turntable in a horizontal plane. When the turntable is not rotating, the pointer points at O; when the angular velocity of the turntable's rotation is ω1, the pointer points at A; when the angular velocity of the turntable's rotation is ω2, the pointer points at B. Suppose none of the springs exceeds the elastic limit. Find the ratio of ω1 to ω2.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the rotating shaft/spring fixed end corresponds to the vertical position at the left end of the ruler, and the transverse graduations of the ruler are uniform. From the positions of the arrows and graduation lines in the figure, it can be read that: point O is 3 equal divisions from the rotating shaft, point A is 4 equal divisions from the rotating shaft, and point B is 6 equal divisions from the rotating shaft. Let the length of each equal division be l, then r_O=3l, r_A=4l, r_B=6l. When the small ball is not rotating, the pointer is at O, indicating that the spring is then at its natural-length position; therefore at A and B the elongations of the spring are respectively Δx_A=r_A-r_O=l, Δx_B=r_B-r_O=3l. Then reason: the small ball moves in uniform circular motion with the turntable, and in the direction along the rod the spring force provides the centripetal force. Therefore at A there is kΔx_A=mω_1^2 r_A, and at B there is kΔx_B=mω_2^2 r_B. Substituting Δx_A=l, r_A=4l, Δx_B=3l, r_B=6l, gives ω_1^2/ω_2^2=(Δx_A/r_A)/(Δx_B/r_B)=(l/4l)/(3l/6l)=1/2. Therefore ω_1/ω_2=1/√2.
